newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada budget seen boosting dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canada budget seen boosting dollar.

text.p: Canada's federal budget next week could be a launch pad for the Canadian dollar's rise this year to four-year highs of about 80 U.S. cents, analysts said on Friday.
"I think the markets are anticipating some very good news from the federal budget," said Michael Gregory, economist and fixed income strategist at Lehman Brothers in Toronto.

Gregory noted that many Lehman customers were saying: "We have been looking for something to point to, some factor which will cause the currency to break out of this C$1.35ish (74 U.S. cents) plus or minus range," Gregory noted.
The Canadian currency has been stuck around 74 U.S. cents so far this year.
Economists said the anticipated good news for the currency was that the government would continue to cut its deficit and might beat its C$17 billion deficit target for fiscal 1997/98.
Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin has pledged to eliminate the deficit, but has given no time frame.
Economists expected Martin to exceed his 1996/97 deficit target by up to C$7 billion, bringing the actual deficit down to C$17 billion or C$18 billion instead of the projected C$24.3 billion.
"I think most people are thinking the underlying numbers are going to show C$16 to C$18 billion. That's what I'm thinking," said Mark Chandler, senior economist at Morgan Stanley in Toronto.
((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
